It seems that this PR doesn't completely remove the regression.
For benchmark, `Perf_Double/TryParse (-1.79(...)e+308)` using Mono JIT on x64
This PR: 428.6 ns -> 363.3 ns (1.179)
The original regression: 267.41 ns -> 371.82 ns (1.39)
I got EgorBo to cancel my previous one, will run another later after I check CI fully succeeds.
Yeah, ok. I think that probably is easiest at this point.

Could it be caused by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/99146? @hamarb123 @jkotas ? It seems to be widespread regression, potentially affecting CoreCLR as well (https://github.com/dotnet/perf-autofiling-issues/issues/30963)

If it is that PR, my guess is it's the following: ```csharp public readonly Span Digits => new Span(DigitsPtr, DigitsLength); ``` since it seems like that probably causes this length check that wouldn't be elided upon further inspection: Presumably, we can fix it to use `MemoryMarshal.CreateSpan` which should fix the issue - is it an intrinsic / not gonna kill me on mono?
My pr https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/102866 seems to have fixed it more or less - please confirm if it fixes the regression fully.

Thank you for the quick fix! 

> Presumably, we can fix it to use `MemoryMarshal.CreateSpan` which should fix the issue - is it an intrinsic / not gonna kill me on mono?

I'm afraid that Mono only intrinsifies the `RuntimeHelpers.CreateSpan`. For `MemoryMarshal` class the `CreateSpan` intrinsic is missing: 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/dad01daffc3fa4e257abe8e33cb9f80fbaff71d7/src/mono/mono/mini/intrinsics.c#L1096-L1105
@fanyang-mono Do you know if we could re-use the `RuntimeHelpers` implementation for `MemoryMarshal` class?

> @hamarb123 Is it possible to use `RuntimeHelpers.CreateSpan` instead?

That's a very different API, it's used to create a `ReadOnlySpan` from a `RuntimeFieldHandle` from a field with `.data` in IL. I think the idea was that we make an intrinsic for `MemoryMarshal.Create(ReadOnly)Span` based on it.

review_comments: This is because the Span ctor has a length < 0 check and MemoryMarshal.CreateSpan doesn't?
Yes - it seems to be the cause based on the regression & the code I'd changed.
